subject: Embedded index sharding playbook for partner integrations

Subject: Embedded index sharding playbook - request and sandbox access

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the intro yesterday. Pinecone engineering is starting a set of partner integrations that embed index shards into hybrid storage topologies (S3 cold lane + vector store hot lane). Before we commit to a pilot, engineering asked if Redwood can share a short runbook / "playbook" that covers recommended sharding patterns, shard sizing heuristics, and fallthrough behavior (when to route to S3 vs index). Key asks from our side: 

- Preferred chunk size and embedding size tradeoffs (tokens -> vector granularity).
- KV cache implications in your runtime when shards are split across stores.
- Expected API rate limits and recommended client-side exponential backoff.
- A short test harness (curl/SDK) we can run in our sandbox to validate cold-lane rehydrate behavior.

We can provision a Pinecone sandbox index and share credentials (Is attached a quick guidelines PDF). If you have a short document or checklist we can iterate on together, that would speed the pilot ramp. Also looping in our consulting partner (Acme) who will run one of the POCs.

Available this afternoon for a 30m alignment — 1pm or 3pm PT work for me.

Thanks,
Amy
Amy Zhou
Partner Solutions, Pinecone

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embedded index sharding playbook - request and sandbox access

Amy — thanks for the clear asks. Im attaching a first-pass playbook (jb_sharding_playbook_v0.1.docx) that outlines our recommended patterns for hybrid index sharding and operational checks. High-level notes up-front:

- Start with 256-512 token chunks (embeddings ~768 dim) for user-facing retrieval; downsample for bulk similarity workloads.
- Maintain per-shard metadata with a warm TTL; hot lane (Pinecone) should handle realtime queries, S3 serves as authoritative cold storage with manifest indexes.
- Runtime will try local KV cache, then hot index, and finally rehydrate from S3 in the background — synchronous fallthrough only for critical low-latency routes.
- For testing, use the attached curl scripts + the Pinecone sandbox link you provided; wel share a small test set (see Drive link) and a short tracing guide for timing observations.

Suggested next steps:
1) Wel sync for 30m today at 3pm PT to align on the test harness and credential handoff.
2) Pinecone to provision sandbox index and share service key to partner-eng@acme-consulting.com.
3) Redwood to run a quick 2-day ingest & smoke test and report latencies.

Im attaching jb_sharding_playbook_v0.1.docx and sandbox-credentials.txt (redacted) for the call.

—Jordan

Looping in a few engineering constraints from our side (short bullets so the POC can be scoped):

- pgvector / self-hosted vector stores: shard manifests must be kept transactionally consistent with the write-ahead log. If writes are batched, include a shard version id to avoid stale reads.
- S3 cold lane: use content-addressable chunk ids (hash of original text chunk + embedding dim) so rehydrate is idempotent.
- KV cache TTLs: keep default warm-window 30s for user chat flows; for high-throughput batch searches set it to 0 to avoid cache thrash.
- When shard sizes exceed ~50M vectors we recommend horizontal shard split and a background index rebuild window (off-peak).

For the test harness: please include a synthetic tail latency test (p95 and p99) and a cold-rehydrate scenario (delete a shard from hot index, query, and validate S3-to-hot rehydrate completes within the expected window).

Also: Ben, can we allocate $5k in sandbox credits for Pinecone test time? Im not sure what the commercial ask will be.

—Vanessa
